newsitem.title: UK: Britain suspends contact with Bosnian embassy.
newsitem.headline: Britain suspends contact with Bosnian embassy.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it was suspending contact with the Bosnian embassy in London.

The Foreign Office said the decision had been taken after Bosnian leaders had failed to meet an August 1 deadline for Bosnia's joint Moslem, Serb and Croat presidency to agree on the appointment of ambassadors.

Western allies agreed in May to impose penalties on Bosnia's joint postwar government unless it reached agreement on the division of ambassadorial posts among the country's ethnic Serbs, Moslems and Croats.
The British decision came at the same time as similar announcements by France and Sweden. Germany suspended contact with the Bosnian embassy there on Sunday.
British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, who visited Bosnia last week, said he had warned the country's leaders of the importance of meeting deadlines set by the Western powers.

"Regrettably they have failed to agree on the appointment of ambassadors by the August 1 deadline," Cook said. "As a result, I am today suspending contact with the Bosnian Charge d'Affaires in London, Mr Mugdim Pasic."
